scope: Vita game BGM/voice bounded file streaming

routes.bgm: knife/src/sound.rs play_bgm queues a physical romfs PathBuf on Vita; end_frame retains one-frame stream start timing and delegates to knife-audio::Audio::queue_stream
routes.voices: knife/src/game.rs scene, replay and configuration voice test use stream_path and file-backed Vita sound calls; desktop still calls Assets::voice and decodes PCM
routes.assets: Assets::stream_path returns a physical .ogg when present, otherwise original Nintendo .opus; stream files are not .mrg archive entries, so no archive range API or persistent duplicate file is needed
routes.fallback: sound effects, movie audio, and desktop BGM/voice still use their existing PCM APIs

decoder.format_detection: Read first four file bytes on mixer worker: OggS uses existing libopusfile AudioStream, otherwise Nintendo Opus uses new Rust file-backed adapter
decoder.nintendo: 48 kHz mono/stereo; validates DATA packet bounds and total frames by bounded sequential scan; seeks with one-second pre-roll; per-packet decode, fixed maximum 8 KiB encoded packet and 5760 stereo sample float scratch via fallible Vec allocation; no whole-file encoded or decoded Vec
decoder.loop: clamps source loop endpoints to actual stream length as desktop PCM path does
limitations: Nintendo Opus initial metadata validation and arbitrary seek scan packets from the file start; memory remains bounded but very long tracks can have startup/seek latency.
Nintendo Opus read was verified against a synthetic fixture and full decoder at selected frame positions; no actual game asset or Vita3K playback was tested in this task.

Vita game full crate cargo check is blocked by its separate glib/gstreamer cross dependency; sound.rs is directly typechecked on Vita using isolated harness, while game.rs Vita audio call edits were syntax-checked.
The native AudioOut worker may play silence during the initial long file scan.
Unexpected looping BGM EOF/error clears the reported BGM state; asynchronous decoder errors are logged by Sound and retained in Audio::last_error.
